_readme: Human rulings on held-out probe misses. SEPARATE FILE BY DESIGN.
The held-out fixture (arch-memory-probes-heldout.json) says, in its own
header, not to edit it to make a gate pass — that would destroy the only
untainted measurement available. But a probe can miss because the FIXTURE
named one acceptable answer when the codebase genuinely has several, and
refusing to ever record that would make the metric permanently wrong in the
other direction.
So rulings live here instead. The fixture stays exactly as authored, the raw
mechanical recall stays reported, and each ruling is attributable and
reviewable on its own.
RULES:
1. A ruling names the SPECIFIC returned symbol judged acceptable. Never a
blanket 'this probe is fine'.
2. `ruledBy` is the human who decided. This is a judgment call, recorded as
one — not a silent metric adjustment.
3. The harness reports RAW and ADJUDICATED recall side by side. A reader
must always be able to see what the machine measured before anyone
ruled on it.
4. Rulings are for 'the fixture named the wrong-but-not-only answer'. They
are NOT for 'the retrieval was bad but I want the gate green'.

rulings.rationale: findingRow takes a single finding and emits an escaped <tr> with severity, pass, file, status and detail cells. The intent was 'format a single audit finding for display in the dashboard'. Source read before ruling; it is arguably a better answer than the a-priori pick (presentFinding).

Closest returned candidate was atomicWriteFileSync, which writes ONE file atomically. The intent requires all-or-nothing across a SET of writes ('cannot leave a half-installed state') — that is what transaction.mjs's journal, rollback and quarantine exist for. A single-file atomic write does not solve the stated problem. Recorded as a real miss; the probe wording was also ambiguous.

Closest returned candidate was receiptPath — six lines that path.join a filename. It records nothing, and the intent was 'record which files an install wrote so it can be undone'. Recorded as a real miss. Note writeReceipt scored 0.752 on a DIFFERENT probe but missed its own, which points at a weak purposeSummary rather than a retrieval defect.
